decisions.statement: The scan, the reading, the times, the ending and the set last said are handed in.
The reading is asked about the processes the scan answered rather than its own.
A process's times are read before that process is ended.
A live descendant stating no acting agent of its own is taken with the process it hangs off.
A descendant stating an acting agent of its own is left to the reading rather than taken.
A process reached twice is ended once.
A process is signalled through the module asking a process to end and then making it.
A stray and a stray's line are said the same way here and by the command naming strays.
The subagents a sweep could not read are said only where that set differs from the set handed in.
A set that gains a subagent, loses one, or empties differs, and is said.
A set handed in that will not be read reads as no subagent.
Every ending is said whatever that set does.
The set a sweep could not read is written where it is read from again.
Nothing here reads a transcript or a page.
No memory and no processor is read to choose what to end.

definition: every stray ended, and each ending said with the times that process took
